newsitem.title: USA: Troops leave California for possible Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Troops leave California for possible Zaire force.

text.p: U.S. Air Force troops from California were sent to European bases on Thursday for possible deployment to Zaire with an international force that would help starving refugees, officials said.

Two transport planes, a C-141 Starlifter and a C-5 Galaxy, left Travis Air Force Base, about 40 miles (65 km) east of San Francisco, on Thursday. More than 50 personnel were deployed, according to Lt. Craig Heighton, a Travis spokesman.
The movements involved aircraft and tanker aircrews that could help to prepare airfield operations in Central Africa.
"This is what we train for and exercise for everyday," Heighton said. "This is the bread and butter of what we do and we're prepared to go anywhere."
Maj. Deb Watros of Travis declined to disclose their destinations in Europe.
"We are pre-positioning troops in the European theatre that would then go to Africa to support the relief effort," Watros said. "We're anticipating being a part of the operation Guardian Assistance."
The troops at Travis are assigned to the 60th Air Mobility Wing, which is part of the U.S. Air Force.

President Bill Clinton tentatively agreed on Wednesday to order U.S. troops to join an international humanitarian rescue mission aimed at helping about 1 million refugees facing starvation and death in eastern Zaire.

Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters earlier on Thursday that Washington would demand at least an informal ceasefire agreement between warring Hutu and Tutsi militia groups around the Zairean border town of Goma before committing troops to the humanitarian aid force.
About 1,000 U.S. troops, including an elite Army airborne battalion based in Italy, could begin flying into Zaire next week, according to a senior Pentagon official.
Canadian, British and French troops are also expected to take part in the mission.

Most of the refugees in Zaire are ethnic Hutus who fled Rwanda after genocidal tribal warfare there in 1994. Rwanda now is controlled by the rival Tutsis, who drove out the Hutus after suffering massacres in the 1994 fighting.
The refugees recently fled their camps along the Zaire-Rwanda border when a Zairian Tutsi group, facing expulsion from Zaire, began attacking Zairian troops.
